samples.evidence: `dropStaleStyleOff` deliberately skips `underline` on runs with an `href` (document.ts:489), and the doc comment calls that out as load-bearing ("The link-underline override is left alone"). The only new setBlockType test (test/model/document.test.ts:~360 'drops a style-off override the new block type no longer defaults') uses a plain non-link run and only exercises `italic`. Grepping the docs test tree for `underline: false` finds exactly one hit (document.test.ts:379, the applyInlineStyle link test) — nothing constructs a link run with `underline: false` and then changes the block type. Deleting the `key === 'underline' && inline.style.href !== undefined` guard would keep every test green, yet it would make underline-off on a link permanently untoggleable after any block-type change.
searchedFor: read new setBlockType test in test/model/document.test.ts

samples.summary: Format painter's effective-value (named-style default) read is untested
samples.evidence: `captureFormatAtCursor` bakes booleans from `raw[key] ?? defaults[key]` (text-editor.ts:3010-3013) and the doc comment states the point: "painting from an italic Heading 6 makes the target italic instead of clearing it". The only new painter test (test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts:843 'Cmd+Alt+V removes a flag the copied format does not have') copies from a plain paragraph whose run carries `italic: true` explicitly, so `raw` alone satisfies it. Dropping the `styleDefaultsAtCursor()` term entirely would leave both painter tests green while a heading source would start *clearing* the target's italic — the regression the comment names. Searched the docs test tree for painter/styleBuffer/Shift+C usages; only the two tests in backward-selection-toggle.test.ts drive this path, both from a non-heading source.

samples.summary: Mixed link/non-link slice behavior of styleOffAsClear is asserted only for the all-link case
samples.evidence: The doc comment (document.ts:426-429) makes a deliberate trade-off: `underline: false` is kept for the *whole* slice when *any* run in it is a link. The new test 'keeps an explicit false when the range carries a hyperlink' (test/model/document.test.ts:~366) applies `href` to the entire range 0..6, so the slice is uniformly a link — the 'any run' aspect (a slice containing one link run plus plain runs) is never exercised, and neither is the collapsed-caret branch of `rangeCarriesLink` (`from === to`, document.ts:38). A change from 'any run' to 'all runs' semantics, or a break in the collapsed-caret condition, would not be caught.
searchedFor: read new applyInlineStyle tests in test/model/document.test.ts:299-420

samples.summary: Dropping the re-assertion of existing attrs in styleByPath has no test for its stated purpose
samples.evidence: `tree.styleByPath([...blockPath, i], { ...existingAttrs, ...styleAttrs })` became `tree.styleByPath([...blockPath, i], styleAttrs)`, justified in the comment as avoiding clobbering "a concurrent remote change to an attribute this patch does not mention". No test in packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts exercises a concurrent/remote attribute change (all applyStyle tests use the single local `store`/`doc`). Single-client attribute preservation is covered incidentally by the pre-existing tests at lines 650 and 723 (`reread` through a fresh store), so the change is not wholly unguarded — but the concurrency property the comment claims is untested, and no test would fail if the re-assertion came back.
